clue.text: Following leads in special operations, spies left party

indicators.note: the leads of the words special and operations are their opening letters, taken here

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: After a secret mission's opening moves, the agents walked out of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a political group the spies leave, but it is the definition: a get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering or get-together, the same thing as a party.

clue.text: Shop initially with two articles to wrap up

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Shop

parts.note: the indefinite article a and the definite article the
the indefinite article a and the definite article the

explanation.surface: A shopper is told that their purchase comes with a couple of items to be wrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe something is to wrap it up in bandages or cloth, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Dreadful cliché about king, concerning history

indicators.note: about tells us the scrambled letters go around the other pieces
dreadful suggests the letters of the word cliché are mangled into a new order

parts.note: R, from Rex, is the usual abbreviation for king
on can mean concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A critic complains of a terrible stock phrase about a monarch in a history book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' looks like a critic's verdict but scrambles the stock phrase into CHICLE, which 'about' wraps round the king and the word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written record of events in order of time, a kind of history.

clue.text: Unknown author takes director in bar with log fire

indicators.note: takes signals that one piece accepts another into itself
in confirms the director piece goes inside the author piece

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, marks a work whose writer is unknown

explanation.surface: An anonymous writer brings a film director into a pub with a cosy log fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but the definition is a metal bar that holds logs in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, or firedog, is one of a pair of metal supports holding logs in a hearth.

clue.text: Successfully woo girl holding diamonds — that can give you a lift

definitions.text: that can give you a lift

indicators.note: holding means the combined pieces enclose another letter

parts.note: to win someone is to succeed in wooing them
lass is a northern British word for a girl
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A suitor wins over his girlfriend with a diamond ring, which really lifts the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' sounds emotional, but the definition is literal: a device for hoisting loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a winch with a horizontal drum used to haul up heavy loads such as anchors.

clue.text: Sort of banal piece's impossible to get away from

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort out or rearrange, applied to the following letters

parts.note: the possessive is read as a plain s ending, giving all its letters

explanation.surface: A dull artwork is said to be everywhere, impossible to avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges BANAL PIECES; the apostrophe in piece's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inescapable cannot be avoided or evaded, so it is impossible to get away from.

clue.text: Rough sleeper holds single record

indicators.note: holds signals one piece wrapped around another

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for someone who sleeps rough
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single

explanation.surface: A homeless man clutches a single vinyl record.
explanation.walkthrough: A dosser is British slang for a homeless person sleeping rough; 'holds' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents, a record kept on a person or subject.

clue.text: Bikini, perhaps, has a price

parts.note: a toll is a price or charge, often to use a road

explanation.surface: A swimsuit comes with a hefty price tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' looks like a swimsuit, but it is the Pacific coral atoll; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands is a ring-shaped coral island, an example of the type.

clue.text: Eagerest to make trip in cheapest place on ship

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters stumble into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The keenest passengers set off on a voyage travelling in the cheapest berth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as a voyage, fitting the ship, but it is the stumbling that rearranges EAGEREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-priced passenger accommodation on a ship, below the decks.

clue.text: Roughen up a certain Mr Pitt with energy

parts.note: Brad Pitt is the American film star
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone wants to rough up a particular Mr Pitt, full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Pitt' suggests William Pitt the British prime minister, but the setter means the actor Brad Pitt.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or wear a surface down by friction, roughening it.

clue.text: Some gent renovated jewel

indicators.note: renovated means remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman has an old jewel refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone is a precious stone cut for jewellery, so it serves as a jewel.

clue.text: Showing respect if no choir performing

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on a show in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A concert-goer remarks that it is a mark of respect if the choir does not sing.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorific title or form of address is one used to convey esteem or respect.

clue.text: Habit of Victorians taking very cheap beer even for them!

parts.note: a farthing, a quarter of an old penny, was the smallest British coin, so very cheap
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Victorians had a custom of drinking extremely cheap beer, even by their standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a custom but means a garment; the farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny, and 'of Victorians ... even for them' is surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A farthingale was a hooped petticoat, and habit can mean a style of dress or garment.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing makes Bette lose head

indicators.note: lose head tells us to drop the opening letter of the surname

parts.note: Bette Midler is the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A worthless person drives the singer Bette to distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Bette brings in her surname MIDLER, and 'lose head' removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who avoids work, a good-for-nothing.

clue.text: One back in rugby team leaving space between locks

parts.note: the centres are back-line players in a rugby team
a parting is a leaving or departure

explanation.surface: A rugby back quits the side, leaving a gap in the scrum's second row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests rugby forwards, but here means locks of hair; a centre is a position among the rugby backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre parting is a line dividing the hair down the middle, a gap between locks of hair.

clue.text: Dig tunnel for redevelopment that's gratifying

indicators.note: redevelopment means the letters are rebuilt into a different structure

explanation.surface: Excavating a tunnel for a regeneration scheme brings satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgent describes giving in to desires, so it is gratifying wishes freely.

clue.text: One looking into the future admitting son may become religious writer

indicators.note: admitting means letting another letter inside

parts.note: a palmist claims to read a person's future in their palm
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A fortune teller who takes on a son may turn into an author of sacred texts.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalmist composes psalms, sacred songs, so is a writer of religious verse.

clue.text: Children's puppet directors win everything

parts.note: Sweep is the grey dog glove puppet from the British children's show Sooty
a company's directors together form its board

explanation.surface: A kids' puppet and a board of directors scoop every prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweep is the squeaking dog puppet partnered with Sooty on long-running British children's television.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep the board is an idiom for winning every prize or contest available.

clue.text: Plain damage I repair

indicators.note: to damage something knocks it out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone who breaks things is also the one who fixes them, plain and simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open grassy plain, as in North America.

clue.text: Ramsey perhaps doubled a source of fodder

indicators.note: doubled means the same piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: Alf Ramsey managed England's 1966 World Cup winning football team

explanation.surface: A man named Ramsey, twice over, supplies animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alf Ramsey was the manager of England's 1966 World Cup winners; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of an Alf.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa, also called lucerne, is a plant grown as hay and forage for livestock.

clue.text: My staff endlessly hard to fathom

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a stick is a staff or walking cane

explanation.surface: Someone's walking stick is impossibly long and baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystic means having a hidden or spiritual meaning beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Grub of regular variety

indicators.note: of signals a word made out of letters lying within the following words

explanation.surface: A standard type of food is on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' reads as food, but it is the insect in its early stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft-bodied immature form of a beetle or similar insect, a larva.

clue.text: Drunk comes up to plant again

indicators.note: comes up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a toper is a habitual heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunkard arrives to replant a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot a plant is to move it into a new pot, planting it once more.

clue.text: Engineer fuelled in US city as a requirement

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY abbreviates New York, the American city

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An engineer refuelled a vehicle in New York because it was needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a person, but it is a verb; its scramble EEDFULL sits 'in' the city's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Needfully means necessarily, done because it is required.

clue.text: August? Put in danger around its beginning

indicators.note: around means the danger verb is wrapped about the extra letter

parts.note: to imperil is to put in danger
its refers back to August, whose first letter is A

explanation.surface: A month is threatened right at its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective meaning stately; 'its beginning' points back to that word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: August means majestic and grand, close to imperial in the sense of regal and magnificent.

clue.text: Person engaging lawyer right in court

indicators.note: in places the legal right inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone hires a solicitor to argue that they were right in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as being correct, but it is the legal right called a lien.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is one who hires the professional services of someone such as a solicitor.

clue.text: Restrained old hooligan given anaesthetic

indicators.note: given here means the hooligan is given a dose, taking the drug inside him

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth often seen as a hooligan
ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A thug from decades ago was sedated and held down.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy, or Ted, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, associated with rowdiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up with a rope, so physically restrained.

clue.text: Ploy to get one caught following diplomacy

indicators.note: following means these letters come after the diplomacy word

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people, diplomacy
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A negotiator's ploy is to win over one person through diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre or scheme to gain an end, a ploy.
